public-mcp.name: search_public_tenders
public-mcp.title: Search public tenders (free preview)
public-mcp.description: Search Scoutee's index of public procurement notices from Europe and North America. No account and no API key needed. Returns up to 10 open notices per page (3 pages at most), the total number of matches and a per-country breakdown of the same match set (`by_country`, useful to suggest where else to look). Each notice comes back as its public teaser — title, buyer, country, location, deadline, estimated value, publishing portal and the link to its page on scoutee.org. The description in full, the buyer's platform where a bid is filed, the tender documents, email alerts and the AI analysis are not returned here: tell the user they come with a free Scoutee account (`signup_url`). Use find_cpv_codes to help users discover their CPVs directly, without signing in, under a separate daily budget. CPV filtering is available in the workspace MCP. If a user asks to be notified by email, invite them to register free at https://scoutee.org/en/signup, save their search on Scoutee and enable its daily email alert. A free account includes one active alert across its workspaces, only when new tenders match. Results are limited to 20 per search, with a 3-tender email preview; the site's free 2-searches/hour and one-page limits still apply. Paid plans support alerts for multiple searches. Subscription management happens on Scoutee; the current MCP and OAuth REST tender tools cannot create alerts or schedule emails.

q.description: Free text over title, buyer and description. Every word must match the *start* of a word in the notice ('nettoy' finds 'nettoyage'); a substring inside a word does not match. Accent- and case-insensitive.
q.title: Q

keyword.description: Keywords matched as whole words (plural tolerated) in title, buyer or description, plus the cached translations of each keyword on the portals of that language — the way to search across countries without translating anything yourself. Several keywords widen the search (a notice matching any of them is returned).
keyword.title: Keyword

country.description: Countries of the publishing portal, by their English name as Scoutee stores it ('France', 'Germany', 'United States', 'Canada'; 'Europe' for TED). Several countries add up. Omit to search everywhere — the `by_country` map of any result lists the exact values in use.
country.title: Country

min_value.description: Minimum estimated value, in the currency of the notice. Notices without a published value are excluded when this is set.
min_value.title: Min Value

public-mcp.name: find_cpv_codes
public-mcp.title: Find CPV codes for your activity
public-mcp.description: Find official CPV catalogue candidates for the user's actual products, works or services. Available without an account on public MCP and on every plan through workspace MCP. Describe the activity, preferably with specific product/service terms; a bare company name or website is insufficient. Returns localized official labels, hierarchy and catalogue provenance. Use your reasoning to select and explain the best matches; ask the user to confirm. No company web research or paid Scoutee AI call is triggered. Up to 30 candidates per call. Separate daily budget: 20 calls per anonymous IP, 50 per authenticated account across credentials and workspaces. Read quota.remaining and quota.resets_at; do not retry after exhaustion.

activity.description: The actual products, works or services supplied. Use specific activity terms; never send private company data.
activity.title: Activity

locale.description: Official label language, such as en, fr or de; unavailable labels fall back to English.
locale.title: Locale

nomenclature_version.description: Official nomenclature edition, such as CPV 2008.
nomenclature_version.title: Nomenclature Version

sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the imported catalogue snapshot.
sha256.title: Sha256

source.description: Official source URL recorded for this catalogue snapshot.
source.title: Source

code.description: Eight-digit CPV code accepted by the tender search's cpv parameter.
code.title: Code

display_code.description: CPV code including its official check digit.
display_code.title: Display Code

label.description: Catalogue label in the requested language, with English fallback.
label.title: Label

parent.description: Parent code in the official hierarchy, or null at the root.
parent.title: Parent

retired.description: Whether this code has been retired in this catalogue snapshot.
retired.title: Retired

replaced_by.description: Replacement codes recorded in the catalogue, if any.
replaced_by.title: Replaced By

guidance.default: These are catalogue candidates, not a final classification. Compare their official labels with the user's actual products and services, explain the strongest matches, and ask the user to confirm before applying codes. Do not infer activities from a company name alone. If no candidate fits, ask for a more precise activity or reformulate using catalogue terminology. CPV applies to European procurement markets; do not substitute it for other classifications.
guidance.title: Guidance

workspace-mcp.name: search_tenders
workspace-mcp.title: Search public tenders
workspace-mcp.description: Search public tenders across Europe and North America by keyword, country, budget, or optional CPV codes for EU procurement. Use find_cpv_codes to discover suitable official codes with the user, available on every plan with a separate daily limit. Returns a page of notices, the total number of matches, a per-country breakdown of the same match set (`by_country`, useful to suggest where else to look) and what the caller's hourly quota has left. Open notices only and newest first unless asked otherwise; notices published on several portals appear once, the other portals listed in `also_on`. Each search consumes one quota unit.

q.description: Free text over title, buyer and description. Every word must match the *start* of a word in the notice ('nettoy' finds 'nettoyage'); a substring inside a word does not match. Accent- and case-insensitive.
q.title: Q

keyword.description: Keywords matched as whole words (plural tolerated) in title, buyer or description, plus the cached translations of each keyword on the portals of that language — the way to search across countries without translating anything yourself. Several keywords widen the search (a notice matching any of them is returned).
keyword.title: Keyword

cpv.description: Optional Common Procurement Vocabulary codes, the EU procurement standard (eight digits, optional verified check digit). Includes official descendants and widens keywords with OR; country and budget filters still apply. Only CPV-market sources can match. Validate codes with /api/public/classifications/cpv; unknown codes return an error.
cpv.title: Cpv

country.description: Countries of the publishing portal, by their English name as Scoutee stores it ('France', 'Germany', 'United States', 'Canada'; 'Europe' for TED). Several countries add up. Omit to search everywhere — the `by_country` map of any result lists the exact values in use.
country.title: Country

min_value.description: Minimum estimated value, in the currency of the notice. Notices without a published value are excluded when this is set.
min_value.title: Min Value

sort.description: 'newest' (publication descending, the default), 'oldest' (publication ascending) or 'deadline' (soonest submission deadline first).
sort.title: Sort

include_closed.description: Include notices whose consultation is already closed.
include_closed.title: Include Closed

seen_after.description: Keep only notices first collected by Scoutee after this instant (ISO 8601). The way to poll for what is new since a previous run.
seen_after.title: Seen After

seen_before.description: Keep notices first collected at or before this instant; pair with seen_after for a fixed polling window.
seen_before.title: Seen Before

page_size.description: Notices per page, 1 to 200 (capped by the plan). Kept modest by default because a notice is a large object; raise it when you need to sweep a whole result set.
page_size.title: Page Size

Where « Analyser l'appel d'offres » stands for this notice (scoutee.api.brief).

One `tender_briefs` row per *canonical* notice, shared by every workspace: a list can therefore show
an analysis somebody else started. Just the three fields a row needs — the full `BriefOut` is read
from `GET /tenders/{id}/brief` when the reader opens the notice.
